Keep everything the Tibetan does not bear on.

The glossary has also changed since the last draft: Tibetan forms were added, and a form inside a longer term no longer counts (citta inside bodhicitta, vajra inside Hevajra). Re-check the glossary hits listed in the input.

Observations on the verse lines from the pass that matched glossary terms to the Tibetan (check them yourself against the input):
- cp.01.1b (kala, sgra gcan): Where the Bengali has kāla the Tibetan song has sgra gcan, 'Rāhu', writing Munidatta's identification of Kāla with Rāhu (cp.01.m2) into the line itself.
- cp.01.5b (dhamana, zla ba): Where the Bengali has dhamaṇa the Tibetan song has zla ba, 'moon', taking over Munidatta's gloss (āli, with the purification of the moon), and its commentary (cp.01.m6) then glosses zla ba, not dhavana, as A li.
- cp.01.5b (camana, nyi ma): Where the Bengali has camaṇa the Tibetan song has nyi ma, 'sun', again taking over Munidatta's gloss (kāli, with the purification of the sun), which its commentary (cp.01.m6) applies to nyi ma.

Observations on the verse lines from the pass that matched glossary terms to the Tibetan (check them yourself against the input):
- cp.10.h1 (raga, glu dbyangs): The Tibetan heading renders rāga as glu dbyangs 'melody', transliterates the name as de sha kha, and adds the poet, nag po spyod pa'i zhabs, whom the Bengali heading does not name.
- cp.10.1a (dombi, g.yung mo): Throughout the song the Tibetan translates Ḍombī with the common noun g.yung mo 'low-caste woman' instead of transliterating the name.
- cp.10.1a (hut, khyim): khyim is 'house, home' rather than a word for a hut, matching Munidatta's tavāgāra 'your house', which cp.10.m2 renders khyod kyi khyim.
- cp.10.1b (brahmin, bram ze'i): The Tibetan has bram ze'i bu 'brahmin's son, brahmin boy' for bāhma nāṛiā, apparently taking nāṛiā as 'lad' rather than 'shaven-headed', in line with Munidatta's cittavaṭuka, which cp.10.m2 renders sems ni bram ze'i bu.
- cp.10.2b (p-kanha, kAh+Na): The verse transliterates the vernacular name (Kāhna), while the heading and the commentary use the Tibetan name nag po spyod pa (see cp.10.m1).
- cp.10.2b (kapalika, thod pa'i): Here kāpāli is rendered adjectivally, thod pa'i rnal 'byor 'skull yogi', whereas 6a transliterates it (ka pA li) and cp.10.m7 has thod pa can.
- cp.10.2b (nirghrna, skyug bro spangs): Rendered analytically as skyug bro spangs, 'having given up revulsion'.
- cp.10.3a (lotus, pad): The Tibetan compresses 'one lotus, sixty-four petals' into gcig nyid pad 'dab 'the one, lotus petals', so the lotus appears only as the first member of the compound pad 'dab (the commentary has the full pad+ma).
- cp.10.3b (dombi, g.yung mo): In this line caṛi 'climbing' becomes der gnas 'staying there' (matching Munidatta's tatra sthitvā), and bāpuṛī seems to be transliterated (pa pu lI'i or pu lI'i after gar byed) rather than translated.
- cp.10.5a (tanti, rgyud): rgyud, a word that also means 'tantra' and 'lineage', renders both tānti here and Munidatta's tantrī in cp.10.m6.
- cp.10.6a (kapalika, ka pA li): Transliterated here (ka pA li), unlike the translated thod pa'i of 2b.
- cp.10.7a (lake, rdzing bu): rdzing bu is 'pond, pool'; cp.10.m8 uses the same word for sarovara and renders kāyapuṣkara as lus kyi rdzing bu 'the pool of the body'.
- cp.10.7b (dombi, g.yung mo): The Tibetan makes Ḍombī the object of 'taking' (g.yung mo blangs nas 'having taken the g.yung mo') and ends bdag gi pha rol gsod 'I kill the other (or: my adversary)', apparently reading parāṇa as para 'other' rather than prāṇa 'life'.

Observations on the verse lines from the pass that matched glossary terms to the Tibetan (check them yourself against the input):
- cp.14.h1 (raga, glu dbyangs): The Tibetan heading renders rāga with glu dbyangs, 'song, melody' ('the melody called d+ha ni sI'), not with a word for passion.
- cp.14.h1 (p-dombi, Dom+bi pa'i zhabs): The Tibetan heading names the poet as Dom+bi pa'i zhabs, a calque of Ḍombīpāda with zhabs for -pāda, where the Bengali heading gives only the rāga; m1 calls him grub pa'i slob dpon Dom+bi pa.
- cp.14.1a (pl-yamuna, ya mu na): The Tibetan transliterates the Sanskrit name Yamunā (spelled ya mu na), not the song's vernacular jaunā.
- cp.14.1b (matangi, gdol pa'i bu mo): The Tibetan does not keep the caste name but has gdol pa'i bu mo, 'outcaste girl', the same phrase m2 sets beside g.yung mo for Ḍombī.
- cp.14.1b (para, sgrol bar byed): Here the whole phrase pāra karei is rendered by the verb sgrol ba, 'ferry across', which also means 'rescue, liberate'; there is no separate word for pāra, which 5a renders pha rol.
- cp.14.2a (dombi, Dom+bi): The song lines keep the name in transliteration (Dom+bi), whereas the commentary at m2 translates it with g.yung mo.
- cp.14.2b (guru, bla ma): sadguru is rendered bla ma dam pa, 'holy guru', here and in m3.
- cp.14.2b (jinapura, rgyal ba'i pho brang): The Tibetan makes the Jina's city a palace (pho brang), and keeps that word in m3, where Munidatta's gloss mahāsukhapura becomes bde ba chen po'i grong khyer, 'city of great bliss'.
- cp.14.3a (keruala, skya ba): The Tibetan has skya ba 'dzin pa lnga, 'five holding oars' or 'five oar-holders', which may read the five as rowers rather than oars, and m4 cites the verse by the same phrase.
- cp.14.3b (gagana, nam mkha'i): The compound gaaṇadukhola is rendered nam mkha'i ko ba, with ko ba ('hide', a leather vessel) for dukhola, and m4 repeats nam mkha'i ko ba for gaganadukholaka.
- cp.14.4a (wheel, 'khor lo): The same 'khor lo serves in m4 for the subtle-body wheels ('khor lo'i phyogs su for cakroddeśena), so the Tibetan does not separate the two senses by wording.
- cp.14.4a (srsti-samhara, bskyed dang sdud pa): sdud pa, 'gathering in', renders saṃhāra in its sense of withdrawal rather than destruction, and m5 repeats the pair as skyed pa dang sdud pa of saṃsāra.
- cp.14.4a (pulinda, bu lin+da): The Tibetan transliterates the word (bu lin+da) rather than translating it, so the translators too seem to have treated it as opaque, and the Tibetan of m5 lacks Munidatta's gloss of it as napuṃsaka.
- cp.14.5a (kabadi, 'gron bu): The Tibetan names only one fare, so the Bengali pair kabaḍī … boḍī is rendered by 'gron bu alone, and it adds Ḍombī (Dom+bi) as the subject of the line.
- cp.14.5b (kula-shore, dogs): As it stands dogs su would mean 'into doubt', but m6 twice has ngogs su, 'at the bank', so dogs is probably a corruption of ngogs, and phan tshun, 'here and there', may render the doubled kulem̐ kula.
